jobs.title: Growth Lead (Paid Marketing)
jobs.description:
ABOUT AVANT ARTE

Avant Arte is a curated platform connecting the world’s leading artists and public arts institutions with a new generation of enthusiasts, collectors and patrons. We collaborate with the most exciting contemporary artists such as Ai Weiwei, Mickalene Thomas, Maurizio Cattelan and Jenny Holzer to create limited editions of the highest quality, from prints and sculptures to digital works.

Our global community of over 4 million collectors and art enthusiasts reflects the growing energy and curiosity of a new generation transforming how art is discovered and supported. Together with leading museums and institutions, we develop fundraising collaborations that strengthen public access to art and engage the new generation of patrons who will shape its future. Make-Ready, our North London print studio, is the largest fine art silkscreen printmaker in the world.

Our mission is to make discovering and collecting art more accessible, connecting artists, institutions and audiences in meaningful ways that expand art’s reach and impact.

OUR CULTURE

We’re a small team with really big ambitions, both for what we want to achieve and also the environment we’re building. We want to create a company that remains thoughtful as we scale and tries to be genuinely progressive in how we operate. We want people to really own what they do and be given the autonomy and freedom to make mistakes, learn, and create something meaningful.

We all work incredibly hard because we really care about what Avant Arte is here to do – we’re looking for exceptional people who are proactive, hungry to learn, and want to put their pride in our collective achievements.

We know that creating an inclusive environment that promotes and values diversity is critical if we want to build something with impact and meaning. We believe that having diversity in age, background, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and perspective will make us an infinitely better company. We were shortlisted for Women in Tech’s Best Employer - Small Company and Best Benefits, and Otta’s top 100 startups to work at. 

WHAT WE NEED

Over the past few years, the marketing team at Avant Arte has become integral to driving some of the business' most important outcomes: acquiring collectors efficiently, making campaigns perform, growing collector value and building a distinctive brand.


This role is responsible for the first two: acquiring new collectors as efficiently as possible, and maximising the commercial impact of every campaign. For us, those things are inherently linked – campaigns are one of the main ways we acquire new collectors, with every release bringing in a mix of new and repeat buyers. This role therefore owns both the acquisition engine and the performance of the campaigns that drive it. 

Alongside Avant Arte, you’ll also be responsible for paid acquisition for Make–Ready Editions – our newer, more accessible editions brand, born out of Make–Ready, our specialist fine art printmaking studio. You’ll work closely with the dedicated Make–Ready Editions Marketing Lead, who owns the brand and wider marketing strategy.

This role sits at the heart of our programme of editions, spanning paid acquisition, audience strategy and measurement through to the planning, forecasting and optimisation of every release. Paid media is also one of the largest single investments in the business. Our spend has increased by more than 300% in the last two years and is set to keep growing. We need someone who can bring the measurement, forecasting and testing rigour that should come with that investment. 

We have, on average, around two releases every week. Two Marketing Managers, who run campaign planning and optimisation day to day, will report into this role. You’ll also work closely with the rest of the marketing team. Brand-building organic social sits with the Brand Lead and Social Manager, while organic activity designed primarily to drive release performance sits with you. CRM and growing long-term collector value sits with the CRM team, who you’ll work with closely.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

Performance marketing & acquisition

  • Lead paid acquisition for Avant Arte and Make–Ready Editions, adapting audience, media and optimisation strategies to the needs of each brand

  • Set realistic targets for each channel and optimise performance to meet these targets in flight

  • Bring much stronger measurement, forecasting and testing discipline to a paid media budget that's growing quickly, with a clear view on what we're getting back for what we spend

  • Make spend calls quickly. Our campaigns are short and the right decision needs to be made in hours rather than after several weeks of clear data

  • Build a testing programme that helps us iterate learnings from one release to the next

Campaign management

  • Set the approach to cross-channel campaign planning and optimisation across our programme of releases

  • Own the cross-channel forecast for every release before it goes live, including the assumptions behind it and what needs to happen for us to hit it

  • Work with the team to brief the creative campaign needs, based on both the artist and what we know will make the release perform

  • Lead the post-campaign analysis and make sure what we learn actually changes the next forecast, paid media plan or creative brief

  • Manage two Marketing Managers who run campaigns day to day, providing direction, supporting their developing and and helping raise the standard of campaign planning and optimisation across the team

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • You've managed meaningful paid media budgets yourself, with deep experience in Meta and ideally experience across channels such as Google and Tiktok too

  • You're comfortable opening Ads Manager, Metabase, Shopify or a spreadsheet and getting to your own answer

  • You understand CAC, ROAS, conversion and incrementality, but you also know where each of those measures can give you the wrong answer

  • You can build a forecast from sensible assumptions, explain why you believe it, and work out why reality differs afterwards

  • You have good creative judgement and can help shape work that performs without compromising how we present the artist or artwork

  • You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information

  • You’ve managed people before, with experience supporting development while giving people clear ownership and accountability

  • You can make a complicated performance problem understandable to people who don't spend their day looking at dashboards

You'll probably have

  • Around 7+ years’ experience in performance, growth or acquisition marketing, including experience managing and developing others

  • Experience in a fast-paced, performance-driven e-commerce or marketplace environment

  • A background that spans both paid performance and campaign or launch planning

  • An interest in art and culture is a plus. You don’t need to come from the art world, but you should be curious about it and interested in applying rigorous performance thinking within a distinctive, creative business

BENEFITS INCLUDE:

  • Generous equity allowance

  • Private Healthcare (UK)

  • Enhanced pension contributions and parental leave policies 

  • 25 days of holiday plus four extra company wide days

  • Supportive of Hybrid/Flexible Working

  • L&D budget of €1000 per year per employee

  • Regular company socials

  • Art loan scheme for employees

jobs.description:
About Ember

We're building the future of public transport — convenient, connected, affordable and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.

We’ve already demonstrated that it's possible to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world. This leads to a massive emissions reduction and is only possible because we control the full-stack and integrate it tightly together. That includes the tech platform, the charging infrastructure and the vehicles themselves. This also means we’re providing a much better passenger experience with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.


We’ve come a long way and there’s much more to come, with the arrival of new vehicles, launch of new routes and hubs to continue to grow our network, it’s a very exciting time for Ember. The challenge is to scale 100x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve already successfully raised equity from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and secured a large debt facility from our ethical banking partner, so we’re looking to build a team that can help us take things to the next level.


The role

This role is all about learning through doing, joining an existing team that takes care of day to day Operations. In the first instance, we're looking for generalist Interns who are keen to get to grips with all aspects of the Operational side of the business.


Sometimes that will mean troubleshooting, but after every fire you'll take a step back and think about how to help the team design and implement a process that could have dealt with the issue proactively.


What you will do

We're still very much a scale-up, so your role will be broad. At a minimum it will include:

  • Day to day involvement in vehicle, driver and route management

  • Looking after our customers across multiple channels

  • Helping to manage vehicle and charger maintenance

  • Assisting with the planning of future routes and expansion

You'll be engaging with a committed Operations team to ensure we have 24/7 coverage. Part of this may mean pitching in and helping with weekend or evening cover in case of incidents, whilst also working to ensure we keep these unanticipated events to a minimum.

Please note - this is an on-site role, and interested parties should only apply if they are able to work from our office in central Edinburgh.


Start dates and timings
We're looking to engage the right applicants for an initial period of three months, starting in October 2026


The long term
We're growing very rapidly, and our hope is very much that our internship programme could lead to permanent roles for the right candidates.


Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.


What’s on offer

This is a paid graduate internship, and conditions will satisfy the requirements of the National Living Wage.


How do I apply?

Apply using the form, providing a CV and a cover letter explaining why you're right for this opportunity. 


How you work and think is much more important to us than any specific industry experience. A genuine passion for climate or public transport, or even both, are also very valuable at an entry level, and we'll teach you the rest. You don't need to be a master of anything but shouldn't feel out of your depth anywhere.


Whether you're a university leaver or a veteran, a recent graduate looking for first-hand experience in Climate and Technology or a frustrated Public Transport enthusiast who would love to make the switch into this industry, we're keen to meet people with a passion to make a real difference.


We look for a range of qualities in all members of Ember's Operations Team, and the following should resonate with you:

  • A strong sense of what good really looks like whatever the topic, problem, or issue. After all, good is good.

  • An instinct and curiosity that draws you to problems and drives you to find a solution, rather than hoping someone else picks it up.

  • An innate structured thinker – everything is a series of steps which can be broken down and rationalised.

  • An ability to build strong relationships with a diverse range of people, from drivers to software developers.

Ember is the UK's first fully-electric, zero-emission coach company. We launched in October 2020 and are now running multiple routes across Scotland – including Dundee to Glasgow, Aberdeen to Edinburgh and connections from Glasgow and Edinburgh up to the west coast.  Other destinations across Scotland will follow in 2026 and 2027.

We're looking for the very best and most eager drivers to join the Ember team. Whether you have a passion for electric vehicles or simply for great customer service, we'd love to hear from you. It’s really important to us that we find people who are truly motivated to be a key part of a company that is proving that things can be done differently.


That means that for the right people, we’re happy to discuss relocation packages to various destinations across Scotland. Right now, that could mean locations such as:

  • Skye

  • Inverness

  • Oban

  • Fort William

We're a fast growing company with a track record of success, so this is an exciting time to join the future of public transport!


Responsibilities

As a driver, you're on the front-line. Not only will you be responsible for keeping the coach moving, you'll also provide on the ground operational support, which means having outstanding communication and organisational skills, proactivity to solve problems when there are delays and acting as the main point of contact for customers if they have any issues or need help. When things on the roads get busy, you'll be thinking one step ahead and will be working super closely with our Operations team to make sure that Ember's commitment to quality is always met.

This is a role for someone who is already at the top of their game as a driver but who is also looking for more responsibility and variety in their day to day. We're looking for forward-thinking drivers who can provide flexibility, and for the right individual there may be opportunities to be involved in the launch of a brand new hub including supporting new drivers coming on board by getting in early.

You should enjoy working with people and take pride in doing what it takes to deliver a great experience (as well as driving of course). That might mean helping someone with their bags, keeping the coach spick and span or making an effort to say a cheery 'hello' when people board.

We've built lots of new technology to help ensure customers get the best experience possible. That means you'll need to be open to learning new systems and using them in the correct way.

As a small business, we put a lot of trust into our drivers. We expect you to take pride in the work that you do and this will involve light cleaning duties throughout the day to keep our coaches in top condition. We are also evolving fast, so love people that want to give input into how we can do things better and who do this in a thoughtful, constructive way.


Benefits

  • £16.50 per hour starting rate.

  • £17.30 per hour after one year - we reward those who want to make a long term career.

  • £17.90 per hour if you become an Ember Ambassador - those who really live our values and give the best passenger experience.

  • Relief contracts are also available - £18.49 per hour (£16.50 base rate plus additional pay in lieu of holiday)

  • Overtime rates starting at £19.80 per hour.

  • Free CPC renewal for full time and part time drivers

  • 28 days paid annual holiday pro rata

  • Flexible annual leave - request your own holiday dates rather than being assigned them

  • Up to 10 days unpaid annual leave pro rata

  • 20 days paid leave for sickness, jury duty, parental or other unplanned leave pro rata

  • Established progression paths at a fast-growing company

  • Referral scheme - get paid for referring other top drivers to us

  • Friendly culture

  • You'll be driving a state-of-the-art electric coach

  • You’ll contribute to a hugely positive environmental impact, with every journey reducing emissions and traffic

Hours

We're running a 24/7 service, seven days per week, and looking for drivers wanting to work a variety of shifts. We'll give you five weeks’ notice of what the rota looks like so you have plenty of time to plan. We also frequently have overtime opportunities available at shorter notice.


Next Steps

Get in touch if you think you might be the right fit or learn more about Ember at www.ember.to


Requirements

You will need to meet these basic requirements:

  • Full PCV licence: Category D as a minimum

  • Up to date CPC and a digital tachograph card (or able to get both quickly)

  • Able to demonstrate high-quality driving, including smooth braking and a commitment to safety

  • Flexibility to work early, late or night shifts on any day of the week. In return, we'll try to make these as sociable as possible and agree them well in advance

jobs.title: Network Analyst - Senior
jobs.description:
We're looking for an experienced analyst to help design and grow Ember's network. You'll find route opportunities, build the timetables that run them, and use data to make every part of the network work better. We care less about which industry you've worked in than about your ability to think clearly, work in the real world as well as in code, and run several things at once to a high standard.

About Ember

We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.

Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation – everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.

We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and 98 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level.

The role

This is a broad, hands-on role where you'll work across the full lifecycle of a route — from spotting an opportunity on a map to launching it, then making it better once it's running. We're a small team with a lot of ownership on offer. You'll decide what needs figuring out, and figure it out.

Finding new routes means going deep on Google Maps, researching existing transport alternatives, getting out into the real world to test ideas, and engaging with local communities to understand what they actually need. You'll need to know what's possible with our fleet of electric coaches and charging infrastructure, and to be comfortable trading off the most attractive-looking route design against the efficient use of those assets. The best route on paper isn't always the best route to run.

You'll also be one of the people shaping where Ember goes next. That means thinking about the network in the medium to long term rather than just individual routes, and being a strong voice in strategy conversations with the founders.

We don't build traditional clock-face timetables that ignore traffic patterns. Ours are probabilistic, accounting for how the use of each stop varies across days, weeks and seasons. You'll design them, take them through council consultation and registration with the Traffic Commissioner, and make sure the resulting service information ends up in the right places — everywhere from Google Maps to the paper timetables in bus shelters.

A great timetable is only the start. You'll work alongside our operations and charging teams to make sure we've hired and trained the right number of drivers, that there are decent rest facilities where they can take breaks, that we have enough vehicles to run the route, and that the charging will be there when it's needed. You won't do any of these things yourself — but you'll be central to figuring out what's needed and communicating that to other teams.

Launching a route is also only the start. Once a service is live, you'll use our data to assess how it's performing and work out how to make it better — sometimes a tweak to the timetable, sometimes a change to a stop, sometimes a deeper rethink. You'll do this in our own tooling: we don't rely on third-party network planning software, and you'll work closely with our engineers to make that tooling better with every route you run through it.

We're serious about AI as a tool. You'll have access to frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others with generous usage limits, and we expect you to use them to move faster on data work and analysis. Being AI-native isn't a substitute for being good — you're accountable for the routes you design and the timetables you launch.

What you might work on

You’ll work on a mixture of greenfield and brownfield projects. That could include:

  • Designing and launching new intercity routes in new geographies — picking the corridor, understanding the existing alternatives, working out charging patterns, building the timetable and getting it registered with the Traffic Commissioner.

  • Re-engineering the timetable on one of our busier routes so we can provide higher passenger utility without adding vehicles, using booking, occupancy and traffic data to find the slack.

  • Building tools that let us run more of the network with less effort — whether that's simulating a proposed timetable against historical demand before we commit to it, or automating the parts of route launch that currently eat days of analyst time.


Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and we offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.


What’s on offer

You'll receive a salary of £55,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home.

How do I apply?

Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you. We like actions over words, so include a link to something you've built that showcases your skills.


Who we're looking for

You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:

  • Statistically literate. You're an expert in spreadsheets, comfortable with the most complex formulas. You know SQL and/or Python. You have a good grasp of statistics and can use it to make sense of messy real-world data.

  • Grounded. You know when a model is telling you something real and when it's overfitting. You know when a statistically robust result is operationally useless — the right answer for a route isn't always the one with the lowest p-value. Good solutions survive contact with reality and then thrive.

  • AI-native. You treat AI tools as another way to apply your skills. You're comfortable using frontier models to work faster and more rigorously, and you experiment with new tools and techniques as they evolve.

  • Detail-oriented and strategic. Our network is complex, with lots of moving parts that depend on each other. You can zoom in to the detail of a single stop or driver shift, then zoom out to see how a change ripples through the wider system.

  • Interested in transport. You don't need to be a bus spotter, but the problems we're solving should genuinely interest you.

  • Hands-on. This isn't a desk job. You'll get out into the network — riding routes, walking stops, meeting council officers — and you're comfortable blending the strategic, the digital and the real world.

  • Self-managing. You can run several projects at once without things slipping, take initiative on what to prioritise, and jump in to help colleagues across the business when they need it.

jobs.title: Senior Hub Developer
jobs.description:
We're looking for a developer to grow Ember's network of charging hubs. You'll find the sites, take them through legals and planning, manage the build and energise them. How you work and think matters more to us than which industry you've worked in. You think clearly, can run several projects at once and are as at home on a site as behind a desk.

About Ember

We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.

Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.

We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and ~100 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level.

The role

Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline.

You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time.

Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative.

Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs.

It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. Even after a site is live, our involvement doesn't stop. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself.

Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.

What's on offer

You'll receive a salary of £55,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites.

How do I apply?

Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you.

Applications close Friday 2 October at 5pm.


Who we're looking for

You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:

  • Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one.

  • Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects.

  • A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to.

  • Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote.

  • Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell.

  • Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely.

  • Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet.

  • A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard.

jobs.title: Coach Builder & Smart Repair Technician
jobs.description:
Ember is the UK's first all-electric coach company. We launched in October 2020 and are now running on more than twenty routes – including Dundee to Glasgow, Aberdeen to Edinburgh and Inverness to Fort William – with several further routes launching later in 2026. We are at advanced stages in developing new charging hubs in Kirkcaldy and Glasgow, with many more sites in the pipeline.

As we accelerate our network footprint across Scotland, we are launching a new maintenance and engineering facility in Dundee.

We’re looking for a skilled, reliable and motivated Coach Builder and SMART Repair Technician to join our electric bus maintenance team. This is a hands-on, varied role suited to someone with a practical background who is comfortable working in a busy workshop environment. You won't be expected to be a fully qualified mechanic, but you'll work closely alongside our team of technicians and play a vital part in keeping our zero-emission fleet on the road.

The ideal candidate will be experienced, energetic and confident with the passion to stay on top of the latest developments in the electric vehicle market. This will be a Dundee-based role - but you’ll also be working closely with the teams in Aberdeen, Livingston and Inverness. We’ll make sure that you’re set up for success, with all necessary training, access to the right vehicle and all of the relevant tools and equipment.

This position sits in the middle of bus cosmetic preservation and heavy vehicle structural layout. You will take the lead on end-to-end ownership of bodywork projects—diagnosing alignments, completing structural adjustments, and carrying out surface prep for the panel wrapping team. We need someone who can assess a vehicle and quickly understand exactly how panels and components need to be adjusted or pulled to sit correctly.

This is a truly unique challenge - our coaches are used more intensively than any other electric vehicles in the world so not every problem will have a solution that can be found in a manual. Instead, your team will need to work closely with the manufacturer, go deep into understanding root causes and think creatively about how we could be avoiding the problem altogether in the future.

We’re looking for a problem-solver who will help to identify and resolve issues quickly, and will relish the challenge of joining a new team that will make our state of the art fleet the best-maintained in the country with the lowest downtime.

If you're practical by nature, take pride in your work, and want to build a career in the growing world of electric vehicle maintenance, this could be the perfect opportunity.


Responsibilities

• End-End Ownership: Scope out, manage, and execute repair jobs from initial diagnosis through to final panel alignment and

wrap-ready delivery.

• Panel & Frame Realignment: Look at commercial body frameworks and instinctively figure out structural variances—knowing

what needs to be pulled, moved, or mechanically adjusted this way or that to achieve true lines.

• Wrap Preparation: Execute light bodywork prep, ensuring panels are correctly filled, blocked, sanded, and degreased to

receive high-quality vinyl wrapping.

• SMART Repairs: Resolve local paint defects, deep scratches, scuffs, and minor panel punctures.

• Resource & Parts Estimation: Evaluate damage early to determine the parts required for completion, minimising downtime.

Estimate job timeframes realistically from start to finish.

• HSE Compliance: Maintain a proactive understanding of Health, Safety, and Environment regulations, safely navigating a

workshop environment dedicated to high-voltage electric coaches.

We currently have a team of fifteen employees dedicated to fleet maintenance. You’ll form part of a department that brings all aspects of our maintenance in-house as we continue to grow.

We use technology heavily in the business, primarily building our own software systems. You'll need to be tech-savvy, open to learning new systems and comfortable using remote diagnostics.



You will need to meet these requirements:

  • Technical Background: Experienced Coach Builder or SMART Repair Specialist, ideally bringing a background working with HGVs, PSVs, or heavy commercial coaches, however alternative experience would also be considered.

  • Structural Instinct: A good eye for vehicle geometry; someone who visualises panel alignments and can correct framework

    distortions independently.

  • Operational Autonomy: A self-starter capable of working under their own initiative without needing step-by-step guidance,

    also with strong time management skills to hit fleet deadlines

  • Health & Safety Literacy: A solid understanding for workplace safety standards, handling of equipment, and awareness of

    active workshop environments.

  • Licence: Must hold a valid UK driving licence.

jobs.title: Senior Expansion Manager UK
jobs.description:
Join a fast-growing company with a purpose! At Fastned, you will actively contribute to accelerating the transition to electric mobility. Together with over 450 colleagues (more than 50  nationalities) across 10 countries, we have big plans: we are building a Europe-wide network of 1,000 beautiful fast-charging stations where electric drivers can charge their cars with energy from the sun and wind. We have recently been voted best charging network in the UK, France, and the Netherlands, a testimony to our drive to offer the best charging experience to EV drivers!

Your role

As a senior member of the UK expansion team, you will drive the growth of Fastned and contribute to our mission: 'Giving freedom to the electric driver".You will work directly alongside the UK Expansion Lead to shape and drive our site acquisition strategy, identifying and securing prime locations, forging strategic partnerships, and continuously raising the bar for how Fastned grows its UK  footprint as we strive towards a European network of 1,000 fast charging stations on prime locations. 

We are seeking a senior professional who brings a strong sense of ownership, professional maturity, and autonomy to the role.

In concrete terms, this means you…

  • Contribute to the UK network development strategy: defining target geographies, site typologies, partnership models, and deal structures that maximise long-term network value.

  • Lead the identification, structuring, negotiation, and execution of new EV charging site opportunities across a wide range of counterparties, including commercial landlords, roadside operators, developers, and local authorities, ensuring every transaction is aligned with the network development strategy, commercially robust, and delivered on terms that meet Fastned's financial performance targets.

  • Lead complex, high-value negotiations independently and with commercial authority, structuring leasehold, freehold, and licence agreements that deliver on both strategic and financial targets, while spearheading our drive towards securing flagship locations across the country. 

  • Own and actively manage a portfolio of contracted and pipeline sites, maintaining rigorous discipline over deal timelines, commercial terms, and internal reporting standards. 

  • Work cross-functionally with design, planning, construction, legal, and operations teams to ensure seamless transition from signed agreement through to live station.

  • Drive continuous improvement of the team's processes, tools, data and market intelligence to prioritise effort on the highest-value opportunities.

  • Have a keen eye for market developments and knowledge of when to take advantage of the right opportunities. This includes monitoring policy development and understanding its impact on our development plans. 

  • Help the team structure and streamline processes as much as possible to maximise effectiveness & efficiency.

  • In this role you need to feel comfortable diving into techno-economic topics (together with our subject experts), as you need to know your part when leading negotiations. Your onboarding will include a variety of “masterclasses” around the topics of e-mobility and fast-charging. 

  • Embrace an ambassadorial approach to representing Fastned externally at industry events and trade shows, as well as during day-to-day negotiations.  

  • Act as a senior thought leader within the UK team: mentoring colleagues, elevating team standards in negotiation and market analysis, and contributing to Fastned's broader European expansion knowledge base.

  • Bring creative, outside-the-box thinking to how we structure partnerships and unlock sites that others cannot. 

We are open to finding our next Expansion Manager in one of the cities mentioned in the vacancy (London, Manchester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Glasgow, Edinburgh, or Newcastle), with regular visits to our London office to work closely with the rest of the team!

Is electromobility new territory for you? No problem! As part of your onboarding, you will take part in a series of exciting workshops where you will learn everything you need to know about electromobility and fast-charging infrastructure.

Who are we looking for

You are a high-impact dealmaker with deep roots in the UK commercial property market and the strategic instincts of a leader. You bring a level of professional maturity that allows you to operate with autonomy, challenge the status quo, and bring others with you. You bring along extensive experience with negotiations in commercial real estate, ideally in site acquisition with private landowners, agents, and governmental bodies.

You are keen to communicate Fastned's vision and values to site owners & real estate companies and support your team in its expansion. Additionally, you tick the following boxes:

  • 5+  years of relevant experience in commercial real estate site acquisition or development, ideally within roadside, retail, infrastructure, energy, or a similarly complex real estate environment.

  • Chartered Surveyor (MRICS), or demonstrable equivalent professional standing.

  • Strong negotiation and problem-solving skills.

  • An established and active network of relevant stakeholders across UK property, including landowners, commercial developers, and local authorities. 

  • Comfortable managing dozens of projects simultaneously, at different stages of development, each with their own deadlines and individual stakeholders. 

  • Outstanding stakeholder management skills.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills: able to present with conviction to both internal leadership and external C-suite counterparts.

  • Open for regular travel within the United Kingdom and occasional travel to continental Europe.

  • You’re an outgoing person who enjoys seeing new places and meeting new people.

Nice-to-have…

  • Directly relevant experience in ultra-rapid EV charging is not a pre-requisite, but it is a positive. 

  • Experience with grid connections and work with DNOs, IDNOs and ICPs. 

  • Experience with the UK planning system (NPPF, permitted development rights) as it relates to EV infrastructure or energy assets.

  • Plus points for previous experience in fast growth companies or renewable energy.

  • Strong financial literacy: you know your way around a financial model, understand yield, IRR, and NPV in the context of a site acquisition, and hold your own in conversations with investment-minded counterparties.

  • Highly motivated to accelerate the energy transition: you genuinely care about contributing to the UK’s drive towards electric car adoption, renewable energy and the improvement of air quality. 

Join us in building a better future

We are on a mission to make a positive impact, but we don't forget to recognise & celebrate our successes, big and small. We put a focus on work-life balance, provide you with genuine work flexibility and have family-friendly policies in place. Our core benefits include:

  • Stock option plan -> we believe in shared value creation.

  • A training and development budget of £2,600 per year per employee, because development and training are important to us, and our sector offers endless opportunities.

  • 29 holidays. Additionally, we give you two mission days you can use to contribute to Fastned’s mission or to support a cause that is important to you.

  • In order to find some new sites & enjoy the EV life, we will provide you with your own EV car with charging expenses covered.

  • A paid pension plan, fully covered by Fastned.

  • Full health and dental cover via  Bupa.

  • Daily commuting costs to the office are reimbursed.

  • Daily vegetarian lunches, snacks, and drinks are provided at our office.

  • Weekly CrossFit classes with a trained professional.

  • Mental Wellbeing with nilo health: Access to a confidential mental health platform offering 1-on-1 coaching with psychologists, group sessions, and a variety of digital self-care tools

  • Physical Wellbeing with Wellhub: Enjoy a sponsored membership providing flexible access to a vast network of local gyms, fitness classes, and premium digital apps for wellness and nutrition.

  • Going the extra mile for parents: We provide you with personalised coaching support before, during, and after parental leave, facilitated by Foundree.

  • Understanding women's health is beneficial for all of us, fostering empathy, improving communication, and creating a more inclusive workplace. That's why we teamed up with Flouria, providing you with quick access to a broad range of women's health professionals.

  • In addition to fun events year-round, we throw notorious Christmas parties, annual ski trips and organise an amazing yearly trip abroad with all employees.

Interested? Apply today!

We would love to have a conversation with you! Apply now, send us your CV and explain in your motivation letter why you’re excited about joining our mission to provide freedom to electric drivers and speeding up the energy transition.

The recruitment process consists of these stages below:

  • A first video call with our recruiter to find out more about Fastned & our company culture;

  • Interview with the Expansion Lead UK to get a clear understanding of the role;

  • A second case-interview with the Expansion Lead UK and another member of the pipeline team;

  • An office visit to meet members of the Expansion and wider London team!

Then, it’s time to welcome you on board to Fastned!

If you have questions or need further information regarding your application, please contact our recruitment team via

Fastned stands for equity and inclusion. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, gender identities, sexual orientations, religions, neurodiversity, disabilities, parental status or any other protected characteristic that makes you unique.

jobs.title: Senior Paid Social Manager – Meta & TikTok, Perspektive Paid Social Lead (m/w/d) · Remote
jobs.description:
Das ist dein Job bei uns

Du möchtest E-Commerce-Brands über Meta und TikTok profitabel zum Wachsen bringen? Paid Social ist bei vielen unserer Kunden der entscheidende Wachstumskanal. Deine Aufgabe ist es, ihn zu verantworten und auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets zu skalieren. Unser internes Team aus Creative Strategist, Copywriting, Grafik, Video- und Landingpage-Spezialisten unterstützt dich dabei.

Wie dein Arbeitsalltag aussehen kann:

Mittwochmorgen. Im Business Manager laufen zwei neue Hooks deutlich über Benchmark. Du erhöhst die Budgets und briefst das Creative Team auf Iterationen der Best Performer. Daraus entsteht ein neues Set aus UGC, Founder Ads und Statics, das wenige Tage später live geht.

Am Donnerstag präsentierst du dem Kunden die Entwicklung der Performance, die nächsten Schritte und deine Vorschläge für den nächsten Funnel. Danach briefst du dein Team, jeder Schritt ist klar verteilt.

Drei Tage nach dem Launch steht ein Performance-Uplift von 30 %, der Account skaliert auf 3.000 € Ad Spend am Tag, profitabel bei stabilem CAC. Genau das ist der Job.

Wofür wir arbeiten

Wir sind einer der führenden ganzheitlichen Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum.

Denn was wir immer wieder sehen: Agenturen und Dienstleister betreuen Brands nischig und siloartig, Kanal für Kanal, ohne Blick aufs Ganze. Dabei bleiben enorme Potenziale auf der Strecke.

Wir verstehen uns deshalb nicht als Dienstleister, sondern als Teil des Unternehmens unserer Kunden. Dafür arbeiten bei EVOLVE 30 Spezialisten in sechs Fachbereichen zusammen, vollständig remote ab Tag 1. Weekly Recaps, Coffee Chats und Team-Events sorgen dafür, dass Remote bei uns kein Einzelkämpfertum bedeutet.

So funktioniert Paid Social bei EVOLVE

Dass Creatives über die Performance entscheiden, ist kein Geheimnis mehr. Wir setzen zudem eine Ebene höher an und entwickeln conversionstarke Angebote und Funnel für unsere Kunden mit. Denn Skalierung entsteht selten nur aus guten Ads, sondern auch aus dem Angebot dahinter.

  • Angebotslogik und Preisstruktur gehören für uns zum Kanal. Jedes Angebot rechnen wir auf Deckungsbeitrag durch, bevor es live geht

  • Landingpages und Funnels bauen wir mit. Ein Ad verkauft nur so gut wie die Seite dahinter

  • Creative Strategist, Copywriter, Grafiker und Videografen im eigenen Haus. Kein Warten auf externe Zulieferer

  • KI als Werkzeug im Alltag. AI ersetzt bei uns niemanden. Du arbeitest damit wie mit einem Junior an deiner Seite, von der Creative-Recherche bis zur Auswertung

Was dich hier erwartet

  • Kampagnensteuerung: Du planst und steuerst die Paid-Social-Kampagnen auf Meta und TikTok, von der Strategie bis zur täglichen Optimierung

  • Skalierung: Du skalierst Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets. Die Zielmetrik ist Profitabilität, nicht Ad Spend

  • Creative: Du entwickelst die Creative-Konzepte mit dem Creative Team. Welche Hooks, Formate und Angebote gelauncht werden, entscheidest du

  • Testing: Du sorgst dafür, dass Hooks, Formate und Narrative laufend getestet werden. Denn ein Gewinner-Creative hält auf hohem Ad-Spend-Level nicht lange

  • Datenanalyse: Du bewertest alle Maßnahmen anhand der Performance-Daten

  • Kunden: Du führst die wöchentlichen Kundenreportings und berätst Kunden ganzheitlich, nicht nur auf Kanalebene

  • Aufbau des Bereichs: Du entwickelst Social Ads weiter, über SOPs, Qualitätsmanagement und die fachliche Führung neuer Teammitglieder

Deine Rolle und deine Ressourcen: Du lieferst die Ideen für Ads und Funnels nach Direct-Response-Prinzipien und entscheidest, was getestet wird. Die Detailarbeit übernimmt das Team aus Creative Strategist, Copywriting, Grafik und Video. Perspektivisch übernimmst du die Verantwortung für das gesamte Paid-Social-Team und entwickelst dich zum Paid Social Lead.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im Performance Marketing mit Schwerpunkt Paid Social, als Hauptkanal und nicht nebenbei

  • Nachweisbare Skalierung von E-Commerce-Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets

  • Tiefes Wissen im Meta Business Manager, idealerweise auch im TikTok Ads Manager. Dazu Routine mit Tracking-Tools wie Triple Whale, admetrics oder Tracify

  • Strategisches Verständnis für E-Commerce und sicherer Umgang mit Margen, Deckungsbeiträgen, CAC und POAS. Du denkst über den Werbekanal hinaus und steuerst entlang des gesamten Kundengeschäfts

  • Verständnis für Direct-Response-Mechanismen, UGC-Formate und Founder Ads. Du erkennst die Systematik dahinter, warum ein Creative verkauft

  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau für Kundenkommunikation und Copy-Bewertung, Englisch fließend für die Arbeit in den Ad-Managern. Idealerweise bringst du erste Erfahrung in fachlicher Führung oder im Mentoring mit

Der Rahmen

  • 100 % Remote, kein Hybrid-Kompromiss

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Zweimal jährlich Team-Events und Workations, in Person und an wechselnden Orten

  • Wöchentliche Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats, damit Remote nicht heißt, den ganzen Tag allein zu arbeiten

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Jobrad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass

  • Steuerfreier Sachbezug von 50 € monatlich als Gutschein deiner Wahl

  • Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

  • Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack

So läuft der Prozess

Deine Bewerbung. Dein Lebenslauf reicht. Wenn wir Rückfragen haben, schicken wir dir einen kurzen Fragebogen.

Erstgespräch. Ein kurzes Video-Gespräch mit Vanessa aus unserem HR. Es geht um gegenseitiges Kennenlernen, Rahmen und Erwartungen.

Fachgespräch. Hier geht es in die Tiefe, mit der Geschäftsführung oder dem Lead deines Fachbereichs.

Finales Kennenlernen. Mit der Geschäftsführung und deinem zukünftigen Ansprechpartner, menschlich und fachlich.

Entscheidung und Start. Wir entscheiden schnell und planen dein Onboarding gemeinsam.

Wie lange das dauert: Wir legen Wert auf einen schnellen Bewerbungsprozess. Zwischen den einzelnen Schritten liegen nur wenige Tage. Wenn du parallel in anderen Prozessen bist, sag uns Bescheid. Dann richten wir uns danach.

Deine Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten

Die ersten zwei Monate. Einarbeitung in die EVOLVE-Methodik und unsere Prozesse. Du übernimmst erste Accounts gemeinsam mit dem Team.

Mittelfristig. Volle Verantwortung für mehrere High-Budget-Accounts. Du steuerst das Paid-Social-Team fachlich und onboardest ein weiteres Teammitglied.

Langfristig. Du führst als Paid Social Lead den gesamten Social-Ads-Bereich, fachlich und disziplinarisch, mit bis zu zehn Personen.

Deine Ansprechpartnerin

Vanessa, unsere HR Managerin, ist dein erster Kontakt und freut sich auf deine Bewerbung.

jobs.title: Senior Rollout Manager (f/m/x) – DACH
jobs.description:
Your mission

IONITY baut ein europaweites Netzwerk von High-Power-Ladestationen auf und betreibt dieses. Als Senior Rollout Manager übernimmst du die Verantwortung für die erfolgreiche Umsetzung mehrerer Ladestandorte in der DACH-Region – von der Rollout-Planung und der Standortvorbereitung über die Bauphase, Inbetriebnahme und Abnahme bis zur Übergabe an Operations. Du überführst komplexe, funktionsübergreifende Projekte in einen planbaren und verlässlichen Rollout neuer Standorte.
Die Rolle verbindet Projektmanagement, Infrastrukturentwicklung und Stakeholder-Management. Du koordinierst interne Teams, Behörden, Grundstückseigentümer, Netzbetreiber, Baufirmen, Installationspartner und spezialisierte Partner auf gemeinsame Meilensteine, Entscheidungen und Qualitätsstandards. Deine Arbeit leistet einen direkten Beitrag zum Wachstum des europäischen IONITY Netzwerks, sowie einem zuverlässigen Ladeerlebnis für Elektrofahrzeugfahrerinnen und -fahrer aus ganz Europa. Jede neue Ladesäule als Ergebnis deiner Arbeit beschleunigt die Verkehrswende und ist ein wichtiger Beitrag für eine emissionsfreie Mobilität.

  • Du übernimmst die ganzheitliche Verantwortung für die Umsetzung eines Portfolios von HPC-Ladestandorten in der DACH-Region, mit besonderem Fokus auf die komplexesten, risikoreichsten oder strategisch wichtigsten Standorte. Über den gesamten Projektlebenszyklus hinweg steuerst du Umfang, Zeitplan, Abhängigkeiten, Risikoexponierung, Kostenrisiken, Qualität, Sicherheit, Compliance und die betriebliche Umsetzungsreife.
  • Du übersetzt die Rollout-Ziele in integrierte Standort- und Portfolioumsetzungspläne, definierst Prioritäten, Reihenfolgen, Meilensteine und Abhängigkeiten und stellst eine klare Governance sicher – von der Standortentwicklung und Genehmigungsplanung über die Bauphase und Inbetriebnahme bis zur Übergabe an den Betrieb.
  • Du führst die funktionsübergreifende Umsetzung über die Bereiche Planung und Genehmigung, Bau, Netzanschluss, Logistik etc. hinweg, treibst zeitnahe Entscheidungen voran, löst Konflikte und stellst sicher, dass kritische Schnittstellen zwischen Grundstück, Tiefbau, Elektrotechnik, Netzanschluss, Installation der Ladehardware, Prüfung und Inbetriebnahme aktiv gesteuert werden.
  • Du steuerst externe Planungsbüros, Auftragnehmer, Installationsunternehmen und weitere Umsetzungspartner direkt, setzt klare Erwartungen, überwachst die Leistung, steuerst die operative Umsetzung sowie kommerzielle Risiken und stellst sicher, dass die Partner die vereinbarten Ergebnisse liefern.
  • Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für das Risiko-, Änderungs- und Maßnahmenmanagement des Portfolios, identifizierst kritische Risiken frühzeitig, definierst Gegenmaßnahmen und führst Wiederherstellungspläne für verspätete, blockierte oder erheblich vom Plan abweichende Standorte. Dabei schützt du Umsetzungsqualität, Sicherheit und Compliance.
  • Du triffst Entscheidungen innerhalb deines übertragenen Verantwortungs- und Entscheidungsrahmens und erstellst klare Entscheidungsvorlagen für den Country Manager DACH, sofern eine Eskalation erforderlich ist. Du stellst tragfähige Optionen, Auswirkungen und Empfehlungen dar und wägst dabei Zeitplan, Kosten, Qualität, technische Machbarkeit und die Anforderungen der Stakeholder gegeneinander ab.
  • Du baust vertrauensvolle Beziehungen zu Behörden, Netzbetreibern, Grundstückseigentümern, lokalen Stakeholdern und Umsetzungspartnern auf und pflegst diese, vertrittst IONITY auch in komplexen Gesprächen professionell und löst Genehmigungs-, Netzanschluss-, Grundstücks-, Bau- und sonstige Umsetzungshindernisse pragmatisch.
  • Du erstellst prägnante und entscheidungsorientierte Berichte für Senior Stakeholder, einschließlich Fortschritt, prognostizierter Termine, Prognosesicherheit, wesentlicher Risiken, Kosten- und kommerzieller Risiken, Partnerleistung, Maßnahmen zur Planwiederherstellung sowie der erforderlichen Entscheidungen, um das Portfolio auf Kurs zu halten.
  • Du etablierst und verbesserst kontinuierlich Rollout-Standards, Governance-Routinen, Vorlagen und Umsetzungsleitfäden. Auf Basis gewonnener Erkenntnisse erhöhst du die Planbarkeit, Qualität, Skalierbarkeit und Umsetzungseffektivität des Rollouts im gesamten DACH-Netzwerk.


Your profile

  • Du bist ein Teamplayer und arbeitest auch unter Zeitdruck mit einem hohen Anspruch an Qualität.
  • Du verfügst über nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Leitung der Umsetzung komplexer Infrastruktur-, Bau-, Energie-, Mobilitäts-, Telekommunikations- oder vergleichbarer Rollout-Programme über mehrere Standorte hinweg, ideralerweise im Bereich HPC Ladeinfrastruktur.
  • Du kannst eine Erfolgsbilanz bei der Übernahme von Ergebnisverantwortung über den gesamten Umsetzungslebenszyklus vorweisen – und nicht nur für einzelne Projektaufgaben oder Arbeitspakete.
  • Du verfügst über ausgeprägte Kenntnisse in Programm- und Projektsteuerung, einschließlich integrierter Planung, Risikomanagement, Abhängigkeitsmanagement, Änderungssteuerung und Reporting auf Senior-Ebene.
  • Du hast Erfahrung in der Steuerung externer Partner sowie in der Einflussnahme auf interne Stakeholder in einer Matrixorganisation. Du trittst sicher auf, stellst bestehende Ansätze konstruktiv infrage, triffst Entscheidungen und eskalierst Themen, wenn dies erforderlich ist.
  • Du verfügst über ein fundiertes praktisches Verständnis der Schnittstellen zwischen Standortentwicklung, Genehmigungsplanung, Tiefbau, Elektrotechnik, Netzanschluss, Inbetriebnahme und Übergabe an den Betrieb.
  • Du kommunizierst klar und strukturiert auf Deutsch und Englisch.
  • Du besitzt einen gültigen Führerschein und bist bereit, regelmäßig mit Teams an den Standorten zusammenzuarbeiten.
  • Du hast Erfahrung in der Umsetzung von Ladeinfrastruktur für Elektrofahrzeuge, Anlagen im Bereich erneuerbare Energien oder anderer dezentraler, kundenorientierter Infrastruktur.
  • Du verfügst über etablierte Arbeitsbeziehungen zu Behörden, Netzbetreibern, Grundstückseigentümern und Baupartnern in einem oder mehreren DACH-Märkten.
  • Du hast Erfahrung mit Schnittstellen zu Hochspannungs- oder elektrotechnischer Infrastruktur sowie mit der Inbetriebnahme und Übergabe in ein operatives Netzwerk.
  • Du verfügst über gute Anwenderkenntnisse in AutoCAD und Microsoft Office, einschließlich fortgeschrittener Excel-Kenntnisse oder vergleichbarer Projektsteuerungs-Tools.
  • Du hast ein einschlägiges Hochschulstudium, eine technische Qualifikation oder vergleichbare berufliche Erfahrung in den Bereichen Ingenieurwesen, Bauwesen, Infrastruktur oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet.

jobs.title: Senior People Operations & Payroll Manager (f/m/x)
jobs.description:
Your mission

IONITY is building the backbone of electric mobility in Europe. Founded by leading automotive manufacturers, we operate Europe’s largest high-power charging network across 24 countries, enabling seamless long-distance travel for EV drivers. With thousands of charging points already in operation and significant expansion ahead, IONITY is evolving beyond charging infrastructure into a broader mobility, energy and digital platform. 

As Senior People Ops & Payroll Manager, you'll ensure IONITY's People Operations and payroll run accurately, on time and with care across our multi-country European setup. This is a hands-on role for someone who knows payroll inside out, enjoys making processes cleaner and more scalable, and wants the admin side of work to feel effortless for employees. 

You'll own the payroll cycle end to end, keep our employee data and lifecycle processes in great shape, and be the go-to partner for our external payroll providers, People Partners and employees. 

What you'll do 

  • Own the monthly payroll process across countries, including preparatory payroll accounting, inputs, handovers and sign-off with external payroll providers.

  • Manage core lifecycle processes (onboarding, leave, offboarding), including work time accounts, eAUadministration and work certificates.
  • Act as a main contact for payroll providers, tax advisors and auditors, and resolve issues quickly and professionally.
  • Spot friction in processes, systems and workflows, then fix it, using automation and exploring AI where they add real value.
  • Support the alignment of employee benefits across countries while respecting local requirements.
  • Partner closely with People Partners and Finance so payroll, reporting and People processes join up.
  • Answer employee questions on pay and HR admin with clarity and discretion.
  • Guide or mentor junior team members, own larger process and system projects, and act as a sparring partner to People leadership.


Your profile

  • 5 years of experience in payroll and People / HR Operations, ideally including German payroll.
  • Experience coordinating payroll across multiple countries, working with external providers. 
  • Strong knowledge of relevant labor law, tax and social security requirements, with a willingness to learn new countries.
  • Hands-on experience with Deel & Personio is a strong plus.
  • A structured, reliable and discreet way of working, with a real eye for detail and deadlines.
  • A pragmatic, improvement-minded approach: you like clean processes, but not bureaucracy for its own sake.

As a Senior Software Engineer (m/f/d) at auxmoney, you’ll join our IT Risk & Pricing team, where we build backend systems and services that support risk decisioning, pricing, and data-driven product logic. The work is backend-heavy, involving complex technical problem-solving and close integration with data/analytics workflows. 
 
In this role, you’ll design and deliver impactful features, help evolve a scalable, resilient architecture, and take end-to-end ownership from concept through production. You’ll work closely with analysts/data scientists, product managers, and business stakeholders to ship high-quality solutions and continuously improve our engineering standards. If you are passionate about writing clean, maintainable code, solving complex technical challenges, and building software that delivers real value, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.


What you can expect:

  • Architecture & System Design: Identify and address architectural limitations, make pragmatic trade-offs, and help evolve systems toward scalability, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Technical Leadership: Act as a trusted technical expert by promoting engineering best practices, facilitating technical discussions, and helping teams align on high-quality solutions.
  • Engineering Quality: Build solutions that are secure, scalable, extensible, and cost-efficient while maintaining high coding and documentation standards.
  • Execution & Delivery: Break down complex initiatives into manageable workstreams and deliver incremental value through iterative development.
  • Impact & Knowledge Sharing: Champion engineering excellence, share knowledge proactively, and support the professional growth of colleagues.
  • Collaboration & Problem Solving: Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders, actively contribute to design reviews, and address root causes of recurring technical challenges.
  • Ownership & Mentorship: Take responsibility for challenging projects and guide team members through technical mentoring and hands-on support.
  • Strategic Thinking & Growth Mindset: Balance short-term delivery with long-term system sustainability and continuously look for opportunities to improve technology, processes, and team effectiveness.


Your profile

  • Backend Engineering Expertise: Several years of hands-on backend development experience with preferably strong proficiency in PHP, particularly using the Symfony framework and Python.
  • System & API Development: Proven experience designing, building, and maintaining robust backend systems in production environments, including strong expertise in developing and integrating RESTful APIs.
  • SQL Expertise: Hands-on SQL experience in application development, with strong proficiency in relational data modelling (table design, keys, and constraints) and writing complex, performant queries to support business features.
  • Cloud & DevOps Practices: Experience working with cloud platforms (preferably AWS) and modern DevOps practices such as CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and infrastructure automation. Experience with Docker and Kubernetes is highly valued.
  • Event-Driven Architecture (Bonus): Familiarity with Kafka or similar event-driven messaging systems is considered a strong advantage.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance: Solid understanding of automated testing strategies, including unit and integration testing, with a focus on delivering reliable and high-quality software aligned with overall quality standards.
  • Product-Oriented Mindset: A strong focus on building solutions that deliver measurable value for users and business outcomes.
  • Team & Communication Skills: Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach, with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams and contribute to a supportive engineering culture.
  • Security & Compliance Awareness: A proactive approach to implementing security best practices and ensuring compliance throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Language Skills: Fluent written and spoken English.

Role

Hive Robotics is building Europe’s first full-stack orchestration platform for unmanned systems: connecting, controlling, and commanding multi-vendor drone and robot swarms. Our RF communication systems are Made in Germany, deployed on active frontlines, and targeting a highly valued tactical communication market with zero sovereign alternatives today.
As our first dedicated Account Executive, you own the sales pipeline: every opportunity from a lead to a signed contract. You take over our existing customer accounts and drive the opportunities our founders and Business Development have opened, with the first new deals expected to close within 3 months. You currently report to the CEO.
This role is customer-facing by design: expect 30–50% travel to customer sites, procurement offices, partners and trade fairs across Germany and Europe, sometimes internationally. The rest of the time you work alongside Engineering, Product Management and our Field Application Engineers.


Responsibilities

  • Own the funnel from the first qualified conversation to signature. Our founders and Business Development open doors with customers, partners and the wider ecosystem. From there the opportunity is yours: you qualify it, drive it and close it, pulling the founders back in only when a deal needs them. Leads you generate yourself count just as much, this isn't exclusively BD's territory.
  • Qualify hard and early. Run discovery against a fixed gate (pain, budget, decision-making unit, timing) before we invest engineering time in a technical deep dive, and keep a clear next step with a date on every opportunity.
  • Lead the customer's buying team through a hardware buying cycle: end users, engineers, procurement, legal and IT, across long evaluations, equipment trials run as projects, integration questions and security reviews.
  • Orchestrate the deal team. Bring in our engineers and Field Application Engineers for demos, trials and technical deep dives, and Product Management for configuration and fit. You decide when a deal needs them and what they're there to do.
  • Own our active customers commercially: account plans, follow-on orders, upsells and expansion into new units and use cases, every escalation that touches the relationship, and regular account reviews with the Field Application Engineer who owns adoption.
  • Turn deployed systems into the next deal: reference visits, customer quotes and case material that you or the founders can use to open new accounts.
  • Own the offer: configuration and pricing, terms and conditions, the cost-benefit case on the customer's own data, and the project plan to signature. Lead our responses to RFPs and tenders where they apply, and build the templates so every proposal starts from a proven base.
  • Get a trial agreement signed before any trial starts: scope, duration, success criteria, pilot price and the path to the main contract. You drive it, Operations owns the paperwork.
  • Close, and hand over cleanly. Request the contract from Operations, keep the customer and the internal side moving, and sign. Then hand over to Operations as a confirmed customer order and to the Field Application Engineer for onboarding.
  • Keep the pipeline honest: stage discipline, forecast and CRM hygiene, and a weekly pipeline review you run for the founders


Requirements

Must Have

  • 7+ years in B2B sales of technical products into complex, multi-stakeholder deals, ideally in a scale up company
  • You have sold hardware, or hardware combined with software and firmware: physical systems with configurations, lead times, integration work and delivery commitments behind them
  • Comfortable selling to technical and non-technical stakeholders in the same room, and knowing when to bring in the engineers
  • Hands-on daily work in a CRM and a disciplined qualification method (e.g. MEDDPICC): your forecast is something the company can plan on
  • Closer's mindset: you treat an opportunity without a next step and a date as a problem, not a pipeline entry
  • Structured working style: your offers, decisions and customer commitments are written down so that Operations, the field team and the founders can act on them without asking
  • Willingness to travel 30–50 % across Germany and Europe, occasionally beyond Europe
  • Fluent English (German is a very big plus)
  • Eligibility and willingness to undergo security vetting for access to some customer sites
Nice to Have
  • An existing network or experience selling to the DACH defense ecosystem: armed forces, procurement offices, primes, integrators
  • Technical fluency in RF communication, embedded systems, unmanned systems, command-and-control or robotics
  • Experience building a sales pipeline or sales function from scratch rather than inheriting one

jobs.description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Le Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.

Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.

Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de quatre ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée.

Ce post-doc est organisé selon quatre axes de travail.

Le premier axe de travail concernera l’utilisation de l’hydrogène pour favoriser la rupture intergranulaire, préalable indispensable à la spectrométrie Auger sur fracture. Ceci permettra d’accéder à des niveaux de ségrégation faibles, insuffisants pour provoquer une fragilité intergranulaire « intrinsèque ». L’hydrogène est connu pour exacerber, dans certains cas, la fragilité intergranulaire. Il s’agira ici d’explorer les conditions dans lesquelles on peut obtenir pour l’acier de cuve des ruptures intergranulaires assistées par l’hydrogène. On pourra notamment étudier l’effet de la concentration d’hydrogène (introduit par chargement cathodique par exemple) et de la vitesse de sollicitation mécanique. La chaire pourra bénéficier ici des compétences du laboratoire sur la fragilisation par l'hydrogène.

Le deuxième axe de travail porte sur le développement d'un modèle quantitatif pour l'analyse par Auger de la ségrégation intergranulaire des éléments d'alliages. Il s'agira d'une approche similaire à celle déjà développée pour le phosphore et le soufre, avec la difficulté supplémentaire de soustraire la contribution du volume, ici non-négligeable.

Les troisième et quatrième axes de ce post-doc s'appuient sur le spectromètre Auger installé en décembre 2025. Cet équipement de dernière génération présente une résolution latérale inférieure à 10 nm. Ceci ouvre de nouvelles perspectives d'analyses que nous souhaitons explorer dans le cadre de la chaire, en particulier concernant l'analyse du carbone et des carbures, qui constitue le troisième axe de travail de ce post-doc. L'analyse Auger de la surface des carbures nanométriques devient possible avec le nouvel instrument et permet d'accéder à la composition chimique des interfaces carbures-matrice. De plus, l'analyse Auger des facettes intergranulaires pourra être faite en-dehors des carbures et permettra d'accéder à la quantification du carbone ségrégé dans le joint.

Enfin, le dernier axe de travail consistera à développer une méthode de quantification de la ségrégation intergranulaire sans rupture. Il s’agira de travailler ici sur une coupe polie du matériau à étudier et à réaliser des analyses locales, par exemple des profils de concentrations à travers les joints de grains.

Compte tenu de l'excellente résolution latérale, on peut ainsi espérer détecter la ségrégation par cette méthode. Une méthode de traitement des données devra être développée pour accéder à des concentrations intergranulaires de solutés. Une telle méthode a déjà été mise au point pour des analyses réalisées par nanoSIMS et pourrait être transposée sur la spectrométrie Auger. Elle permettrait de s’affranchir de la nécessité d'obtenir une rupture intergranulaire (particulièrement limitante en spectrométrie Auger), tout en conservant une préparation d’échantillon très simple (coupe polie) et une productivité potentiellement importante (grand nombre de joints analysables dans un échantillon donné).
